title: Close launches returned to the backlog

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-358#close-launches-returned-to-the-backlog

Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: SEED-358#close-launches-returned-to-the-backlog (.planning/seeds/SEED-358-dashboard-launch-history.md, plan .planning/slice-plans/625-close-launches-returned-to-the-backlog/PLAN.md), implementation revision 55d98f1798541575ab3448e9eafa65deefb9388f.

Promise: the tracked-execution closure reads three published outcomes. A story still in Taken leaves the launch open after its quiet `completed` report; a story returned to the queue closes it as returned. Seed text: "Unchanged: a story still in Taken ... leaves the launch open". Key example: "A tracked execution lands a retained increment and reports quiet completion while its story stays in Taken awaiting wrap-up: it stays open, as today." The caller's suggestion held up against the seed and the code, so I used it unchanged.

Fault: in dashboard/server/completionClosure.ts `trackedExecutionClosure`, I replaced `return listed.list === takenHeading ? "open" : "returned";` with `return "returned";`. The closure then ignores which list holds the entry and reads any listed story as returned to the queue. Fixtures and assertions were left as they were.

Maintained check examined: dashboard/backend-tests/sessions/agent-completion-returned-closure.spec.ts, test "a quiet report closes a launch whose story returned to the queue, keeping that outcome with the report". Its `stillTaken` launch is planted with backlog `{ taken: [story] }` through plantedExecution, receives a quiet `completed` report through deliverReport, and is then checked with `expect(closureOf(keptExecution(dashboard, stillTaken))).toEqual(open)` at line 83.

Command, run from the isolated scratch worktree at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/41a88e64/tmp/intent-coverage (detached at 55d98f179, after npm ci and `node scripts/setup-native.mjs check` passed):
env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES node node_modules/playwright/cli.js test --config dashboard/backend.playwright.config.ts dashboard/backend-tests/sessions/agent-completion-returned-closure.spec.ts --reporter=list

Evidence:
- Pre-probe state: `git status --short` was empty, with HEAD at 55d98f1798541575ab3448e9eafa65deefb9388f.
- Baseline: 2 passed (6.8s). Both tests in the spec ran, including the one that holds the `stillTaken` case.
- Faulted run: 1 failed, 1 passed (2.7s). The failure is at spec line 83, the `stillTaken` assertion. The earlier `back` assertion at line 81 passed, so the run reached the Taken case after a successful returned closure.
- Wrong behaviour: Playwright printed the received record for the `stillTaken` launch as `doneAt: "2026-11-14T16:45:53.520Z"` and `returnedToBacklog: "b8a5db39-…"`, where `open` (both undefined) was expected. The launch's persisted record was therefore closed and marked returned to backlog even though its published backlog lists the story in Taken. That is the promised behaviour going wrong on the intended path. This observation comes from the received side of the maintained assertion, which reads the kept launch record. No separate scratch witness was added, because the received record is the stored behaviour itself.
- The early-binding test still passed under the fault. That is expected, because it plants only a returned story.
- Restoration: an `INT`/`TERM` trap was armed before the edit, and the original file was copied back right after the faulted run. Afterwards `git diff` was empty and `git status --short` matched the pre-probe state (empty). The restored rerun passed 2 tests (1.9s). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force` on that path only. The execution checkout was not edited. It currently shows ` M dashboard/tests/dashboardTest.ts`, which is not from this probe.

Caught by: the maintained assertion `expect(closureOf(keptExecution(dashboard, stillTaken))).toEqual(open)` (spec line 83). This claim covers only the delivery path of a quiet report for a claimed tracked execution whose published story is in Taken. I did not probe the binding path for a Taken story, or the alternative reading in dashboard/src/sessionShown.ts (`returnedToBacklog === completion.receipt`).

Next proof action: none needed for this promise on the delivery path. If more coverage is wanted, the next probe could target the "Returned to backlog" reading in dashboard/src/sessionShown.ts.

Prior dispositions: none matched; the probe causes no new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured, from the Playwright runner's summaries: baseline 6.8s, faulted 2.7s, restored 1.9s, 11.4s in total. This excludes npm ci and native setup check, which were not timed separately.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable. There is no separately supported token or turn measure.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 79831 ms (measured), from 1794674714000 to 1794674793831 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision: 55d98f1798541575ab3448e9eafa65deefb9388f (024a7f4a0 adds only the plan's execution-complete record).
Evidence: the report above; the maintained `stillTaken` assertion caught the scratch fault on the delivery path.
Decision: no follow-up. The verdict is Caught, with no assertion gap or missing test path; the unprobed "Returned to backlog" reading has its own maintained unit assertion (session-reading-rule.spec.ts) whose mutation was observed to fail during execution.
Canonical follow-up links: none.
